rows.why_long: Underdog higher 69.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 62% (fanduel 84.5, moved to this line). Averaging 98.9 over the last 8 games, higher than 69.5 in 37% of them (raw 63%, shrunk 62%). GB is league-average vs RBs → projects 88.2 (raw 60%, shrunk 62%).
why_points: The pick: Rush yds higher 69.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 84.5, moved to this line) is 62%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 83.5. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 58, 84, 45, 124, 40, 54, 58, 98. Weighted average 98.9; went higher than 69.5 in 3 of 8 games (37% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 62.3 vs 74.8 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±26.6, so the line is 1.1 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Teammate out: +6.6 car with Kyle Monangai OUT. When a lead player sits, his teammates pick up about half his work (NFL 2019-25), so this prop is scaled +43%.
Matchup: GB is about league-average against RBs.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -5% on his average.
PFF: GB plays man on 22% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 24%); he gains 1.14 yds/route vs man and 1.25 vs zone → +0% from scheme.
PFF: GB allows 1.23 yds/route to RBs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.19) → +1% against his usual opponents.
PFF: CHI's run blocking vs GB's run defense: 1.2 yds before contact per carry expected (his usual 1.5, league 1.2); he adds 3.0 after contact → -5% per carry.
Projection: we expect 88.2 rushing yards on average; in a typical game 75.9 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 6.4 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 63% and the matchup 60%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 62%, matchup 62%.
Bottom line: we give it 62% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +6.0 points; that works out to about +11¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
